title: Full macroscopic thermalization and the formation of Schrödinger's cats by unitary time evolution in the weakly perturbed Ising model - Applications of the Roos-Sugimoto-Teufel-Tumulka-Vogel theory
abstract: We study macroscopic thermalization in the ferromagnetic Ising model with a weak generic (highly nonlocal and many-body) random quantum perturbation. We prove that a single typical perturbation makes every initial state $|Φ(0)\rangle$ in a specified energy shell thermalize: a measurement of a large class of macroscopic observables in the time-evolved state $|Φ(t)\rangle=e^{-i\widetilde H_Lt}|Φ(0)\rangle$ yields their thermal equilibrium values, within a prescribed precision and with overwhelming probability, at sufficiently large, typical times $t$. The result covers the full finite-temperature range, including the ordered phase, where we use plus boundary conditions. With periodic boundary conditions in the ordered phase, every energy eigenstate in the shell is shown to be an almost balanced macroscopic Schrödinger-cat state. Moreover, every pure initial state becomes such a cat at sufficiently large, typical times, with each branch in the corresponding macroscopic thermal equilibrium. The proof combines the theory of Roos, Sugimoto, Teufel, Tumulka, and Vogel with rigorous Ising large-deviation estimates.
summary: This paper establishes a rigorous quantum-mechanical proof that the weakly perturbed Ising model undergoes full macroscopic thermalization via unitary time evolution. It demonstrates that initial states approach thermal equilibrium values for macroscopic observables and, crucially, that the system evolves into a macroscopic Schrödinger's cat state in the ordered phase. The methodology combines advanced quantum theory with rigorous statistical mechanics estimates.
main_problem: To rigorously prove that a quantum system, evolving unitarily, achieves macroscopic thermal equilibrium and forms Schrödinger's cat states, even when starting from an arbitrary initial state.
main_result: The paper proves that for the weakly perturbed Ising model, any initial state thermalizes to the correct equilibrium expectation values, and in the ordered phase, the state evolves into a balanced superposition (Schrödinger's cat state) of the two macroscopic phases.
method: The proof combines the Roos–Sugimoto–Teufel–Tumulka–Vogel theory with rigorous Ising large-deviation estimates, analyzing the decay of non-equilibrium projections.
model_or_system: The system is the ferromagnetic Ising model, described by a Hamiltonian $H_L$ (with periodic or plus boundary conditions) perturbed by a weak, generic, highly nonlocal random quantum perturbation. The dynamics are governed by unitary time evolution $e^{-i\widetilde H_L t}$.
key_observables: Macroscopic observables (sums of Pauli operators), the non-equilibrium projection $P_{neq}$, and the imbalance observable $B_L$ quantifying the superposition between two magnetization sectors.
important_parameters: The finite-temperature range ($ eta$), the system size $L$, and the perturbation strength $\lambda_L$. The results distinguish between the disordered ($ eta \le  eta_c$) and ordered ($ eta >  eta_c$) phases.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the perturbation being random and highly nonlocal, and the proof requires the perturbation strength $\lambda_L$ to be sufficiently small.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing general thermalization bounds for various observables (including linear combinations) in different phases, culminating in the proof that energy eigenstates and typical-time states are almost perfectly balanced Schrödinger-cat states in the ordered phase.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, purely unitary mechanism for thermalization, which is a major theoretical goal in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, offering insights into how quantum coherence is lost into thermal equilibrium.
